What happens to my Spotify when I die?

By the Afterkeep research team · Reviewed on 26 Oct 2026

Short answer: Spotify doesn't publish a dedicated process for deceased users. With the login, family can cancel Premium (it runs to the next billing date, then switches to free) and close the account; after a 7-day reactivation window, Spotify starts deleting the data. Without the login, contact Spotify Support. If Premium is billed through a phone or internet provider, cancel with that provider.

Key facts

  • No dedicated deceased-user process published
  • Cancelled Premium runs to the next billing date
  • Closure: 7-day reactivation window, then deletion
  • Partner-billed plans are cancelled with the partner

How do I prepare my Spotify account?

  1. Note your Spotify login email in your digital estate plan, and keep the password in a password manager with emergency access.
  2. Want playlists kept? Tell family which ones, before anyone closes the account.
  3. After a death, with the login: go to Manage your plan and select Cancel subscription. Premium stays until the next billing date, then the account switches to free.
  4. Then close the account with 'Close your account and delete your data'. Spotify emails a link that can reactivate it within 7 days; after that, deletion begins.
  5. No option to change the plan? It's billed through a partner such as a mobile or internet provider. Use the contact link under Payment on the account page.
  6. Without the login: contact Spotify Support through its help site and explain the account holder has died. Stop the card or bank payment through the bank too.

Read the official policy ↗

What documents do heirs need?

  • With the login: nothing else
  • Without it: the account's email; Spotify publishes no document list, so have the death certificate ready

How long does it take?

Cancelled Premium lasts until the next billing date. After closing, the account can be reactivated for 7 days; then deletion begins. The same email can be used for a new account 14 days after closing.

What can't be recovered?

  • Purchased audiobooks and future live tickets, when the account is closed
  • Playlists and saved music, once the data is deleted

Frequently asked questions

What happens to my Spotify when I die?

Spotify doesn't publish a dedicated process for deceased users. With the login, family can cancel Premium (it runs to the next billing date, then switches to free) and close the account; after a 7-day reactivation window, Spotify starts deleting the data. Without the login, contact Spotify Support. If Premium is billed through a phone or internet provider, cancel with that provider.

How do I cancel a dead person's Spotify Premium?

With the login, go to Manage your plan and select Cancel subscription. Without it, contact Spotify Support and stop the payment through the bank.

Does closing a Spotify account delete everything?

Yes, after 7 days. Spotify emails a reactivation link that works for 7 days, then starts deleting the data. Purchased audiobooks and future live tickets are lost.

What about a Spotify Family plan?

If the plan manager dies, cancelling moves any managed accounts to the free plan. Members keep their own accounts and playlists.

Why can't I cancel on the account page?

Spotify says that means the plan is with a partner company, like a mobile or internet provider. Find their contact link under Payment.
